name: save_skill
description: Render and save a skill into the configured skills directory. Simple skills are saved as a single .skill file; complex skills are saved as a directory package (SKILL.md + resources + subskills/). Bundle scripts, examples, references, and archives through `resources`: use inline `content` for small UTF-8 text, `content_base64` for small binary data, or `from` to copy an existing file or directory recursively without inlining it. Use proactively to persist reusable skills. Never create or edit `.skill` or `SKILL.md` files with `write_file`/`apply_patch`; save_skill owns the package layout and reserved paths. Saving a package for a name that already exists as a single `.skill` file deletes that old file. Updating replaces the manifest fields: pass every supported field you want to keep. For an existing package, omitting both `resources` and `subskills` updates only SKILL.md and keeps its files; a manifest-only save cannot downgrade a package to a single-file skill.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for distilling session experience into a reusable skill:
- Gather evidence first with search_overflow (past turns) and knowledge_search (saved facts); quote behavior, not project specifics.
- Generalize before saving: no absolute paths, hostnames, tokens, or single-project identifiers; state goal, inputs, steps, and done criteria.
- Iterate safely: save_skill with dry_run=true previews the rendered skill without writing; validate_skill checks the exact arguments; only then save without dry_run.
- Bundle assets through `resources`: `content` for small UTF-8 text, `content_base64` for small binary, or `from` to copy a file/directory tree byte-for-byte. Do not paste large files or archives into `content`.
- Never create or edit `.skill`/`SKILL.md` files with `write_file` or `apply_patch`; save_skill owns the manifest and package layout.
- Updating replaces the manifest fields, not a field-by-field merge: read the existing `source` manifest first, then pass every supported field you want to keep. For a package, omitting both `resources` and `subskills` updates only SKILL.md and keeps the existing files. `load_skill` omits `tools`, `tool_groups`, `mcp_servers`, and `priority`; `disable_*` and `excludes` are not accepted by save_skill.
- Prefer validate_skill over re-saving to fix drafts, and delete_skill to remove a bad skill.

name.description: Skill identifier used in the YAML front matter (and default filename).

description.description: Short summary shown in skill lists and matching.

prompt.description: Full skill prompt body (Markdown). Saved after the YAML front matter.

system_prompt.description: Optional additional system prompt text to include in the YAML front matter.

tools.description: Explicit tool names that the skill is allowed to use.

tool_groups.description: Tool groups that the skill is allowed to use (e.g. builtin, executor).

mcp_servers.description: Required MCP server names needed to run this skill.

priority.description: Optional match priority; higher values take precedence.

file_name.description: Optional output filename for simple single-file mode (forces .skill suffix, sanitized). In package mode this field is IGNORED — directory name is derived from `name` via safe_skill_dir_name; do not rely on file_name to name the package directory.

overwrite.description: Whether to overwrite an existing file/directory at the target path (default: true; set false to fail instead of overwriting). Overwriting is permanent — the previous version is deleted, not kept as a backup.

dry_run.description: When true, validate and render the skill without writing anything; returns the preview plus warnings.

resources.description: Optional bundled resources to save alongside the skill. Each entry has `path` plus exactly one source: `content` (UTF-8 text), `content_base64` (binary bytes), or `from` (copy an existing file or a directory tree, binary-safe). When any resources or subskills are provided, the skill is saved as a directory package (SKILL.md + resource files).

path.description: Relative destination inside the package, e.g. 'references/api.md' or 'scripts/helper.py'. A directory import is copied under this prefix. Must not be absolute, contain '..', be 'SKILL.md', or start with 'subskills/'.

content.description: UTF-8 text to write. Provide exactly one of content/content_base64/from.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded bytes, for small binary resources. Provide exactly one of content/content_base64/from.

from.description: Existing file or directory to copy. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; absolute paths are allowed. Files are copied byte-for-byte. A directory is copied recursively under `path`; symlinks and VCS metadata are skipped/rejected. Provide exactly one of content/content_base64/from.

executable.description: Mark a single-file resource executable (Unix). Directory imports preserve source modes.

references.description: Convenience alias for resources under references/. Same entry shape as `resources` (content, content_base64, or from). Merged with `resources`.

examples.description: Convenience alias for resources under examples/. Same entry shape as `resources` (content, content_base64, or from).

scripts.description: Convenience alias for resources under scripts/. Same entry shape as `resources` (content, content_base64, or from). Use `executable: true` for inline scripts that must be runnable.

subskills.description: Optional sub-skills to save nested under this skill's package (saved as subskills/<sub-name>/SKILL.md). Allows splitting a complex skill into focused sub-skills that can be activated independently. Each sub-skill requires `name` and `prompt`; may also include `description`, `system_prompt`, `tools`, `tool_groups`, `mcp_servers`, `priority`, and `resources`.

resources.description: Resources for this sub-skill. Same entry shape as the top-level `resources` (content, content_base64, or from).
